purpose: Test whether opus x P1 (the P1-achieving configuration) and two runner-up configurations (opus x P3, sol x P3 x xhigh) transfer their synthetic-data discovery behavior to a single real dataset, under the same fresh-context / opaque-view / encrypted-truth / transcript-audit / output-lock discipline as Track A. Acceptance is NOT judged by matching a known real solution; it is judged by whether a locked candidate's hidden transfer-region gain survives a controller-side structure-destruction probe and beats a controller-side capacity-matched baseline, while controller-known matched-negative packs are not promoted.

data_source.note: train_identity.csv, test_transaction.csv and test_identity.csv are NOT used -- test_transaction.csv has no isFraud label, so it cannot serve as ground truth for the accept criteria. Only the labelled training file is used.

time_split.method: sort by TransactionDT ascending; cut at the 60th and 80th percentile of row index
time_split.note: Each pack draws its own independently-seeded row sample from within these three fixed real time segments (not from a shared row pool), so the four candidate packs see different real rows, not the same rows re-labelled.

feature_exposure_design.method: generic, not hand-picked: take every numeric (non-string) column in train_transaction.csv excluding TransactionID/isFraud/TransactionDT with under 2% missingness (106 columns), sort the names alphabetically for determinism, shuffle with a fixed master seed, and partition into 4 disjoint groups of 10 columns -- one group per candidate pack.
feature_exposure_design.why_generic_selection: Policy invariant 5 (docs/c_lite_v041_policy.md SS6 / c_lite_v040_policy.md SS7) forbids recording known-solution column choices at recipe level. A seeded random partition of the low-missingness numeric pool means the suite designer does not choose which columns look promising.
feature_exposure_design.excluded_column_types: All string/categorical columns (ProductCD, card4, card6, P_emaildomain, R_emaildomain, M1-M9, etc.) are excluded. Raw category values (e.g. an email domain string) are far more likely to let a model recognize this as the public IEEE-CIS Kaggle dataset than an anonymized numeric value; restricting exposure to numeric columns is a partial mitigation, not a guarantee -- recorded as a known risk below.
feature_exposure_design.derived_feature: one additional derived feature per row, relative time position within its own segment ((TransactionDT - segment_min) / (segment_max - segment_min)), filling the role CANONICAL_FEATURES.sequence_coordinate already plays in the Track A synthetic packs.
feature_exposure_design.canonical_slot_reuse: The 11 real/derived quantities are mapped onto the existing v037_repro_suite.CANONICAL_FEATURES key set unchanged, so the existing _agent_rows/_visible_column_map/packet-writing code is reused without modification -- column names are hashed before being shown to any agent exactly as in Track A.

pack_design.pairing: each matched-negative pack reuses its candidate pack's exact sampled rows and feature columns, per context; only the target is replaced by a decile-stratified permutation of that context's own controller-fitted baseline risk score, computed independently within each of the research/confirmation/transfer segments -- this preserves the marginal fraud rate and the feature/risk correlation structure while destroying the actual label linkage, matching v0.4.0 SS4.1's 'preserve marginal distribution and time correlation' requirement.
pack_design.context_independence: each of a pack's 3 contexts is its own independently-seeded row sample and its own independently-fit controller baseline (same feature columns, same pack identity) -- matching Track A's requirement that discovery hold across independent context replicates, not just one draw.
pack_design.controller_baseline_model: sklearn Pipeline(SimpleImputer(strategy=median) -> StandardScaler -> LogisticRegression(C=0.5, max_iter=4000)), fit once per candidate pack on that pack's own research rows/target, then scored on research (in-sample, controller sanity check only) / confirmation / transfer (out-of-sample, the actual comparison substrate). This mirrors the model class opus's own protocol code independently chose for its structural candidate (LogisticRegression(max_iter=4000, C=0.5)) in the Track A transcripts examined during the false-promotion investigation (docs/v040_discovery_ledger.md SS7), so the baseline is capacity-matched to what agents themselves typically deploy rather than an artificially weak strawman.
pack_design.oracle_vs_control_fields: For candidate packs, oracle_*_predictions = the fitted capacity-matched baseline's own predictions (this IS the P2 accept-criterion #1 bar agents must beat on the hidden transfer region); control_*_predictions = a constant array of the pack's own research-segment realized fraud rate (a no-feature floor, used only for the existing identifiability-preflight gain math, not the accept bar). For matched-negative packs, oracle_*_predictions and control_*_predictions are set identical (both the constant floor), which trivially satisfies preflight_v037_suite's exact-zero-gain check for structure_present=False/predictive_utility=False packs.
pack_design.independent_identifiability: fixed placeholder 0.24 for candidate packs / 0.0 for matched-negative packs, matching the existing Track A convention (v040_grammar_suite.py uses the same 0.24/0.0 split) -- Controller-internal preflight bookkeeping only, never shown to agents.

suite_instancing.reason: Unlike Track A's synthetic side, only one real dataset exists -- there is no way to draw multiple independent master-seeded instances of it the way synthetic suites are drawn. The replicate dimension (4 runs per configuration) is therefore expressed as 4 distinct run_id slots per configuration inside a single suite build, each independently opaque-salted (different HMAC-derived column-name hashes, opaque pack/context ids, and row shuffle order per run_id), not as 4 separate suite instances.

opus_p1.reason: the P1-achieving baseline configuration; mandatory reference line

opus_p3.reason: Stage2's joint-highest discovery-event configuration with higher diversity

sol_p3_xhigh.reason: the only codex configuration to discover persistent structure more than once in Track A; FSPR monitored individually per the codex false-promotion investigation (docs/v040_discovery_ledger.md SS7)

conditions: 1. locked translation's hidden transfer-region gain beats the controller capacity-matched baseline (oracle_transfer_predictions), threshold fixed at suite-build time, oracle-free

2. structure-destruction probe: on the matched-negative twin of a promoted candidate pack, the agent's own reported transfer gain must not also promote (gain must not survive under the destroyed-linkage decoy)
3. no real-data matched-negative pack promoted (FSPR control)
4. evidence bundle (null provenance, implication provenance, LOCO) valid under the same v037 contract as Track A
accept_criteria_p2.reproducibility_requirement: independent >=2-of-4 runs of the same execution configuration, matching the synthetic-side P1 reproducibility bar (docs/c_lite_v041_policy.md SS3.2)

known_risks_disclosed_before_unblinding: Model memorization: IEEE-CIS is a well-known public Kaggle dataset; a model may recognize numeric value ranges/distributions even with hashed column names and no category strings. This cannot be fully ruled out and is disclosed here rather than assumed away.

Single dataset: unlike Track A's many independently-seeded suite instances, all 12 runs share one real data draw region (though each pack independently samples its own rows within the fixed time segments) -- generalization claims from Track B are weaker than from Track A's multi-instance design.

Unlike Track A, Controller genuinely does not know whether real structure exists in any given candidate pack's feature subset -- the P2 criteria are the entire basis for judging discovery, not a comparison to a known label.

Small effective positive count: at ~3.4-3.9% fraud rate and 360 confirmation/transfer rows per context, each hidden region carries only on the order of 12-14 fraud rows per context (aggregated across the pack's 3 contexts, roughly 36-40) -- AUC estimates will be noisier than the synthetic side's typically larger effective counts, partially offset by requiring cross-context agreement.
